_doc:
THE KINZIE KINSHIP, RULED — T-0732.

James Kinzie's card carried, in free text and citing nothing, the sentence 'He is a half-brother to John H. and Robert A. Kinzie.' T-0597 turned the John H. half into a graded, reciprocal `kin` row on both records, resting on Hurlbut's bracketed note of 1881 (bk_afc_015). The Robert A. half stayed a sentence, and this file is the adjudication of it.

THE ANSWER IS THAT THE ROBERT A. HALF IS NOT WRITABLE, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE ONE THE TICKET EXPECTED. The ticket was filed on the fear of a duplicated pair — two Robert Kinzie households and two John H. Kinzie households, and a `kin` row aimed at the wrong one of a duplicated pair being worse than no row at all. That fear is answered and answered in the affirmative: T-0839 folded both pairs, so there is exactly one Robert and exactly one John H. to aim at. What stops the row is the kinship itself. No source this project holds states a relationship between James Kinzie and Robert Allen Kinzie, and the sources it does hold cannot be chained into one without supplying a fact none of them gives.

NOTHING HERE ASSERTS A NEW IDENTITY, PROMOTES A GRADE, OR ADDS A `kin` ROW. It records a finding and a refusal, and it marks an uncited sentence as uncited.

questions.question: Are `hh_kinzie_r_a` and `hh_kinzie_robert_a` one man minted twice by two passes, or two people? And `hh_kinzie_j_h` beside `hh_kinzie_john_h`?
questions.answer: ONE MAN EACH, both pairs, and the ruling is already landed rather than made here.
questions.settled_by: T-0839, 2026-09-05, rule C2, in data/residents/card_merge_rulings.json clusters `kinzie-robert` and `kinzie-john`; executed as the merge cards data/residents/merged/hh_kinzie_r_a.json and hh_kinzie_j_h.json, with the redirects in data/residents/index.json `merged`.
questions.why_it_holds: The two folded cards are civic mints off press initials — `kinzie_r_a` from 'R. A. Kinzie' at chicago_democrat_1833_12_10#c008, `kinzie_j_h` from 'J. H. Kinzie' at chicago_american_1835_06_20#c005 — and each carries an initials string that no other Kinzie card in the set carries. T-0839's ground for the Robert merge is that no other Kinzie card holds the letter R at all; for the John merge, that 'J. H.' agrees with John Harris and no card and no source reached reads James Kinzie with a middle initial.
questions.corroborated_here: The Democrat advertisement the R. A. card was minted from is a THIRD-PARTY naming, not a signature: John Wellmaker's Man Trap is 'one door north of Mr. R. A. Kinzie's Store', and the extraction records the man's role as 'the storekeeper next door', occupation merchant. Robert Allen Kinzie's own card is a merchant at his own store. That is the trade and the premises agreeing with the initials, independently of the initials, which is what the C2 merge needed and did not cite.
questions.residual: Four Kinzie household cards now stand where the ticket counted six: hh_kinzie_james, hh_kinzie_john_h, hh_kinzie_john_s, hh_kinzie_robert_a. The count could yet fall to three — see `related_finding` below — but that is the owner's call and not this ticket's.

questions.question: Is the James Kinzie / Robert A. Kinzie half-brotherhood writable as a reciprocal `kin` pair?
questions.answer: NO. No held source states it, and the two sources that touch it cannot be chained without supplying the one fact neither gives.
what_the_corpus_holds: bk_afc_015 (Hurlbut, Chicago Antiquities, 1881; data/research/books/claims/american_fur_company_hurlbut.json): '[The late James Kinzie, formerly of Chicago, and half brother of the late John H. Kinzie.]'. It says HALF. It does not say WHICH parent the two men share.

bk_hub_048 (Hubbard's Autobiography, 1911, describing 1818): at Mr Kinzie's house Hubbard met 'Mrs. Kinzie; their eldest daughter, Mrs. Helm; their youngest daughter, Maria ... and their youngest son, Robert'. data/research/books/crosswalk.json merges that Robert into this project's Robert Allen Kinzie (T-0501, claim_id bk_hub_048) and refuses 'Mr. Kinzie' against John Harris Kinzie because he is the elder John Kinzie, dead in 1828 and held here by no record (T-0501, claim_id bk_hub_049).

bk_hub_040 (same source): John H. Kinzie is the Mackinaw clerk 'whose father then resided at Chicago', which is how crosswalk.json's T-0501 merge carries him to John Harris Kinzie. His FATHER is the elder John Kinzie. His mother is named by nothing this project holds.
questions.the_chain_and_where_it_breaks: Robert Allen Kinzie is a son of the elder John Kinzie and his wife — that much is held, cited and already ruled on. To reach James from there the row would need Hurlbut's 'half' to be a shared FATHER, and Hurlbut does not say so. Take the other reading and the tie does not merely weaken, it disappears: if the parent James shares with John H. is the mother, then James is no son of the elder John Kinzie, and he and Robert have no parent in common at all. So the corpus does not establish that James Kinzie and Robert A. Kinzie were brothers of any degree, let alone half brothers.
questions.and_the_degree_is_not_optional: `data/residents/index.json` vocabulary.kin_relations keeps `brother` and `half_brother` apart, and tools/validate.py's RESIDENT_KIN_INVERSES will not let one stand as the mirror of the other. That rule exists because HALF is exactly what a summary flattens. A row written here would have to pick a degree the sources do not give, which is the flattening the rule was built to catch, arriving by the front door.
questions.what_would_reopen_it: Any source that names James Kinzie's parents, or that states in as many words a relationship between James Kinzie and Robert A. Kinzie. Andreas's Kinzie genealogy and Wau-Bun's family pages are the obvious places and neither is read into this project's claims layer yet.
questions.action_taken: The free-text sentence on hh_kinzie_james.json persons[0].note is marked as the uncited claim it is, and points here. No `kin` row is added to hh_kinzie_james.json or hh_kinzie_robert_a.json; hh_kinzie_robert_a.json still carries no `kin` block, which is now a recorded decision rather than an omission.

shared_surname_rule: Nothing here is merged, linked or graded on a shared surname. data/research/books/crosswalk.json refuses 'the Kinzies', 'Mr. John Kinzie', 'John Kinzie' and 'Mrs. Kinzie' against this project's residents for exactly that reason, and its rule governs this file.

related_finding.what: The card `kinzie_john_s` is named from a DIGIT, and the ruling that referred it to the owner was argued on a middle initial the source does not print.
related_finding.evidence: chicago_democrat_1833_12_10#c012 reads, as transcribed, 'TO LOAN, / JOHN 8. KINZIE, / [F]orwarding & Commission [MERCHANT] / CHICAGO—ILLINOIS.' The as_printed string the extraction records is 'JOHN 8. KINZIE'; 'John S. Kinzie' is the extractor's normalisation of it. The trade printed beside the name is forwarding and commission merchant, which is John Harris Kinzie's own trade on his own card, from his own 1834 advertisement.
related_finding.why_it_matters: card_merge_rulings.json's kinzie-john cluster refers `kinzie_john_s` against `kinzie_john_h` to the owner under R3, and its stated ground against the merge is that 'the middle initial S contradicts H'. If the 8 is an OCR artefact of the letter it stands in for, there is no S to contradict anything and the question is an OCR repair rather than a judgement call. This is the same digit-for-letter fault T-0721 is open on for '8. G. Abbot', 'A. 8. Perry' and 'James I1. Gabbs' — a fourth instance, on the surname the project has already named as its trap.
related_finding.not_acted_on_here: The merge was referred to the owner and stayed referred while this ticket ran: T-0732 neither made it nor argued for it, and filed the finding as its own ticket so it would be ruled rather than rediscovered.
related_finding.ruled_by: T-0844, 2026-09-10, which folded T-0854 in and settled both halves. The 8 is a digit-for-letter artefact and the S is unwitnessed, so the R3 ground 'the middle initial S contradicts H' rests on a token the source does not set; what is left is 'John [unread]. Kinzie, forwarding and commission merchant', which is rule C3 — a bare forename onto an anchor — corroborated by the trade INDEPENDENTLY of the initials, the same corroboration Q1 above cites for the R. A. Kinzie merge. `kinzie_john_s` is folded onto `kinzie_john_h`. Q1's residual is spent: the four Kinzie household cards are three.

reading_this_file: Q1 answers the prior question the ticket said had to be settled first. Q2 is the ruling. F1 is a finding made in passing and handed on. Nothing in data/structures/, data/assets/ or the geometry is touched by any of it.
